questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather, the academic reputation of the university, that rent would not be over 6.500 dkk and that it was outside of the EU

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UT was very helpful in putting together online ressources and it was very easy to book an appointment with them if needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: after arrival I recieved some help answering questions about registration for classes, but otherwise i mostly just figured it out myself and asked my housemates

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a collegehouse and would warmly recommend, rent is cheaper than dorms, you do labor to compensate for part of the price and that means a communal feel and meals!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's actually quite nice, but do make sure to live within walking distance from UT if you don't have access to a car, as the transportation isn't great

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: register online, before classes begin, can be a bit confusing to understand the system and the holds

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: meeting with advisor, which is also required to take the courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty successful! one course I wanted was cancelled, but i got a waitlist course in my first week of class

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy! relax, it seems quite overwhelming but you don't know till you know, and waitlists do work!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The quality was so-so, half my courses were great, the other half, felt a little superficial and the professors were just not natural teachers

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: depends on the course, some were hard, some were a bit easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: See this i loved, i felt very much more engaged, lots of quizzes, assignments, readings we actually commented on and interacted with the professor, depends on bigger or larger class, but i like that there is stuff to do underway (multiple exams) instead of the readreadread listen do a little and boom exam at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cognition
psychology of consciousness
adolescent development
intro to develoopmental psy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would very much recommend everything apart from adolescent development, the other 3 were pretty engaging and hard good professors, a different way of seeing things, dev psy was online but one of the best online classes i have had, very nicely designed with breakout discussions and interactive polls

questions.answer: Insurance! be aware how expensive this is and you cannot waive it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food is about the same as DK, be aware that the target by UT is upcharging

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs and spirit orgs, go for a walk during the first week of classes and they will have stands for any interest under the sun

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: use the gym at greg! join a club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: explore austin. Outside of austin i went to round rock, big bend, lano and tubing in san marcos, there is much to do and see

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: extremely easy, but i am also half american. Even with that, I needed to get used to the how are you's and the very polite culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be friendly and open, most people i met were very interested and open with me, and that is different than DK, embrace it!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did find the chattyness and the southern hospitality a bit startling at first, but you might grow to love the little chats with strangers and saying thank you to the bus driver

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: see above

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much before going, it will work out with the classes. don't just hang out with fellow exchange students as many do, take this oppurtunity to immerse yourself in the culture and see what a weird and wonderful place the US can be

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to make friends who you don't live with, so join an org or a club

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, feeling closer to my heritage, the absolute immersion and openness i experience, austin is a beautiful place and the people are very warm mostly

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having a car, do rent one if you can, there is so much to see and do that is just not accessible without a car, i was lucky enough to have friends to drive me places, but it's hard in the beginning

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
